core.title: Abstracting Imperfect Information Away from Two-Player Zero-Sum Games
core.summary: This work shows that certain regularized equilibria do not possess the aforementioned non-correspondence problem -- thus, computing them can be treated as perfect-information problems and yields a simplified framework for decision-time planning in two-player zero-sum games, void of the unappealing properties that plague existing decision- time planning approaches.

core.title: Quick Fixes for Novice Programmers: Effective but Under-Utilised
core.venue: UK & Ireland Computing Education Research Conference
core.summary: This paper uses the associated Blackbox dataset to investigate how quick fixes are used by novice programmers, and finds that users are faster and are more able to make productive progress when quick fix support is available, especially for fixing imports.

The community engagement course and action network: strengthening community and academic research partnerships to advance health equity
core.summary: Evaluation of the network’s processes, infrastructure, and operation provides early lessons learned to strengthen the network and the implications and potential for advancing implementation science through this and similar networks are great.

core.title: Machine Learning-Based Automated Grading and Feedback Tools for Programming: A Meta-Analysis
core.venue: Annual Conference on Innovation and Technology in Computer Science Education
core.summary: An in-depth analysis of how machine learning (ML) has been used to grade and give feedback on programming assignments is provided, including a backward snowball search using the ML papers from an ongoing systematic review and selected 27 papers that met the inclusion criteria.

core.title: The Update Equivalence Framework for Decision-Time Planning
core.summary: This work introduces an alternative framework for decision-time planning that is not based on solving subgames, but rather on update equivalence, and derives a provably sound search algorithm for fully cooperative games based on mirror descent and a search algorithm for adversarial games based on magnetic mirror descent.

core.title: An eye tracking study assessing the impact of background styling in code editors on novice programmers’ code understanding
core.summary: It was found that there was no difference between plain Java, highlighted Java or Stride in terms of correctness, or speed to produce correct answers – and this was unaffected by whether users had seen the latter two interfaces before.

core.title: A Standardized Approach for Collection of Objective Data to Support Outcome Determination for Late-Phase TB Trials.
core.venue: American Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine
core.summary: Standardized methodologies, such as the PPTR approach, could facilitate unbiased efficacy outcome determinations, improve discrimination between outcomes that are related and unrelated to regimen efficacy, and enhance the ability to conduct pooled analyses of contemporary trials.

core.title: Increase Your Statistical Confidence
core.venue: Technical Symposium on Computer Science Education
core.summary: This in-person workshop will help any researchers who use frequentist statistics and want a firmer understanding of the underlying principles: what is a p-value, what does statistical significance really mean, what are the confidence intervals, what is good practice and what should be avoided?

core.title: Novel Hendra Virus Variant Detected by Sentinel Surveillance of Horses in Australia
core.summary: In silico and in vitro comparisons of the receptor-binding protein with prototypic HeV support that the human monoclonal antibody m102.4 used for postexposure prophylaxis and current equine vaccine will be effective against this variant.

core.title: Mastering the Game of No-Press Diplomacy via Human-Regularized Reinforcement Learning and Planning
core.summary: This work introduces a planning algorithm that regularizes a reward-maximizing policy toward a human imitation-learned policy and extends it into a self-play reinforcement learning algorithm called RL-DiL-piKL that provides a model of human play while simultaneously training an agent that responds well to this human model.

core.title: A Unified Approach to Reinforcement Learning, Quantal Response Equilibria, and Two-Player Zero-Sum Games
core.summary: This work studies an algorithm that is inspired by mirror descent and the non-Euclidean proximal gradient algorithm, and demonstrates the virtues of magnetic mirror descent as both an equilibrium solver and as an approach to reinforcement learning in two-player zero-sum games.

Human-AI Coordination via Human-Regularized Search and Learning
core.summary: This work develops a three-step algorithm that achieve strong performance in coordinating with real humans in the Hanabi benchmark, and uses a regularized search algorithm and behavioral cloning to produce a better human model that captures diverse skill levels.

core.title: Emergency remote instruction in 2020: Differential impacts on science, technology, engineering, and mathematics students’ confidence and belonging, by gender, race/ethnicity, and socioeconomic status
Human-level play in the game of Diplomacy by combining language models with strategic reasoning
core.summary: Cicero, the first AI agent to achieve human-level performance in Diplomacy, a strategy game involving both cooperation and competition that emphasizes natural language negotiation and tactical coordination between seven players, is introduced.

core.title: Biaxial Low-Temperature Superplasticity of AA 5083 Produced by Accumulative Roll Bonding
core.venue: Journal of materials engineering and performance (Print)

core.title: Equilibrium Finding in Normal-Form Games Via Greedy Regret Minimization
core.summary: Empirically, experiments on large randomly generated games and normal-form subgames of the AI benchmark Diplomacy show that greedy weights outperforms previous methods whenever sampling is used, sometimes by several orders of magnitude.

core.title: A Fine-Tuning Approach to Belief State Modeling
core.summary: An inference-time improvement framework for parametric sequential generative modeling methods called belief fine-tuning (BFT), which enables, for the first time, approximate public belief state search in imperfect-information games where the number of possible information states is too large to track tabularly.

core.title: Safe Search for Stackelberg Equilibria in Extensive-Form Games
core.summary: This paper presents a theoretically sound and empirically effective way to apply search, which leverages extra online computation to improve a solution, to the computation of Stackelberg equilibria in general-sum games.

core.title: Scalable Online Planning via Reinforcement Learning Fine-Tuning
core.summary: This work replaces tabular search with online model-based fine-tuning of a policy neural network via reinforcement learning, and shows that this approach outperforms state-of-the-art search algorithms in benchmark settings.

core.title: Learned Belief Search: Efficiently Improving Policies in Partially Observable Settings
core.summary: Learned Belief Search is presented, a computationally efficient search procedure for partially observable environments that uses an approximate auto-regressive counterfactual belief that is learned as a supervised task.

core.title: A review of the clinical assistant workforce at a district general hospital during the COVID-19 pandemic
core.summary: A new workforce of clinical assistants (CAs), comprising predominantly of medical students, began work at Northampton General Hospital in April 2020, and was perceived to improve continuity of care, reduce clinician workload and felt significantly more confident with practical and administrative tasks.

core.title: Estimated US Infection- and Vaccine-Induced SARS-CoV-2 Seroprevalence Based on Blood Donations, July 2020-May 2021.
core.venue: Journal of the American Medical Association (JAMA)
core.summary: Based on a sample of blood donations in the US from July 2020 through May 2021, vaccine- and infection-induced SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence increased over time and varied by age, race and ethnicity, and geographic region.

core.title: Pneumococcal Disease Outbreak at a State Prison, Alabama, USA, September 1–October 10, 2018
core.summary: A pneumococcal disease outbreak caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae serotype 12F occurred in a state prison in Alabama, USA among 1,276 inmates, 40 cases were identified and prophylaxis for close contacts included azithromycin and 23-valent pneumococCal polysaccharide vaccine.

core.title: Toward Effective Courseware at Scale: Investigating Automatically Generated Questions as Formative Practice
core.summary: This paper evaluates data for AG and HA questions that students used as formative practice in their university Communication course and shows that the first generation of AG questions perform equally well as HA questions in multiple important respects.

core.title: Racial disparities in invasive Haemophilus influenzae disease — United States, 2008–2017
core.summary: While NTHi causes the largest Hi burden overall, AI/AN populations experience disproportionately high rates of Hia and Hib, with the greatest disparity among AI/AN children aged <5 years.

core.title: Off-Belief Learning
core.summary: Off-belief learning (OBL) is presented, which can be scaled to high-dimensional settings with a fictitious transition mechanism and shows strong performance in both a toy-setting and the benchmark human-AI&ZSC problem Hanabi.

core.title: Descriptive evaluation of antibody responses to severe acute respiratory coronavirus virus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection in plasma and gingival crevicular fluid in a nursing home cohort—Arkansas, June–August 2020
core.summary: Nursing home residents had detectable SARS-CoV-2 antibodies in plasma and GCF after infection and noninvasive GCF may be useful for detecting and monitoring immunologic responses in populations unable or unwilling to be phlebotomized.

core.title: Quality improvement project: Improving documentation and junior doctor confidence on covid-19 ward rounds using a ward round pro forma
core.summary: A ward round proforma is implemented across three wards of a tertiary hospital containing high risk COVID-19 patients, aiming to improve both documentation rates and subsequent ease in finding pertinent information.

core.title: No-Press Diplomacy from Scratch
core.summary: An algorithm for action exploration and equilibrium approximation in games with combinatorial action spaces and evidence that this agent plays a strategy that is incompatible with human-data bootstrapped agents is presented, presenting the first strong evidence of multiple equilibria in Diplomacy.

core.title: Modeling Strong and Human-Like Gameplay with KL-Regularized Search
core.summary: This work introduces a novel regret minimization algorithm that is regularized based on the KL divergence from an imitation-learned policy, and shows that using this algorithm for search in no-press Diplomacy yields a policy that matches the human prediction accuracy of imitation learning while being substantially stronger.

core.title: The impact of signposting and group support pathways on a community-based physical activity intervention grounded in motivational interviewing.
core.summary: Both pathways produced similar improvements in PA and mental well-being; however, the addition of a control would have provided further insight as to the effectiveness.

Health and education concerns about returning to campus and online learning during the COVID-19 pandemic among US undergraduate STEM majors
core.summary: Students' concerns about returning to campus and online learning from home are examined and universities should address student concerns and provide resources to overcome barriers to effective learning.

core.title: Unlocking the Potential of Deep Counterfactual Value Networks
core.summary: It is shown that while a reimplementation of DeepStack loses head-to-head against the strong benchmark agent Slumbot, Supremus successfully beatsSlumbot by an extremely large margin and also achieves a lower exploitability than DeepStack against a local best response.

core.title: Estimated Community Seroprevalence of SARS-CoV-2 Antibodies — Two Georgia Counties, April 28–May 3, 2020
core.venue: MMWR. Morbidity and mortality weekly report
core.summary: The relatively low seroprevalence estimate in this report indicates that most persons in the catchment area had not been infected with SARS-CoV-2 at the time of the survey, and continued preventive measures, including social distancing, consistent and correct use of face coverings, and hand hygiene, remain critical in controlling community spread.

core.title: Human-Level Performance in No-Press Diplomacy via Equilibrium Search
core.summary: An agent for the no-press variant of Diplomacy that combines supervised learning on human data with one-step lookahead search via external regret minimization and achieves a rank of 23 out of 1,128 human players when playing anonymous games on a popular Diplomacy website is described.

core.title: DREAM: Deep Regret minimization with Advantage baselines and Model-free learning
core.summary: DREAM is introduced, a deep reinforcement learning algorithm that finds optimal strategies in imperfect-information games with multiple agents that converges to a Nash Equilibrium in two-player zero-sum games and to an extensive-form coarse correlated equilibrium in all other games.

core.title: South Carolina Conference Journal (MEC) 1887
STEM undergraduates’ perspectives of instructor and university responses to the COVID-19 pandemic in Spring 2020
core.summary: To be prepared for future emergencies, universities should devise evidence-based policies for remote operations and all instructors should be trained in best practices for remote instruction.

core.title: Assessment of commercial SARS-CoV-2 antibody assays, Jamaica
core.summary: The performance of the Roche Elecsys(R) Anti-SARS-CoV-2, Abbott Architect SARS-CoV-2 IgG, Euroimmun SARS-CoV-2 IgA, Euroimmun SARS-CoV-2 IgG ELISA, and Trillium IgG/IgM rapid assays was evaluated in Jamaica shows comparable diagnostic sensitivities and specificities for all testing platforms assessed and limited utility of these tests for persons

core.title: Turning Chutes into Ladders for Women Faculty: A Review and Roadmap for Equity in Academia
core.summary: Enacting policies that function as "ladders" rather than "chutes" for academic women is essential to even the playing field, achieve gender equity, and foster economic, societal, and cultural benefits of academia.

core.title: Exploring the acceleration of Nekbone on reconfigurable architectures
core.venue: International Workshop on Heterogeneous High-performance Reconfigurable Computing
core.summary: This paper explores the porting of Nekbone's AX kernel, a widely popular HPC mini-app, to FPGAs using High Level Synthesis via Vitis, and a comparison and set of techniques that both apply to Nekbone on FPG As specifically and are also of interest more widely in accelerating HPC codes on reconfigurable architectures.

core.title: GGOS Bureau of Networks and Observations: Network Infrastructure and Related Activities
core.summary: The GGOS Bureau of Networks and Observations works with the IAG Services to advocate for the expansion and upgrade of space geodesy networks for the maintenance and improvement of the reference frame and other applications, as well as for the integration with other techniques, including absolute gravity and sea level measurements from tide gauges.

core.title: Combining Deep Reinforcement Learning and Search for Imperfect-Information Games
core.summary: Results show ReBeL leads to low exploitability in benchmark imperfect-information games and achieves superhuman performance in heads-up no-limit Texas hold'em poker, while using far less domain knowledge than any prior poker AI.

core.title: How Teacher Perceptions Influence Social Emotional Learning (SEL) Program Implementation

core.summary: This paper proposes two different search techniques that can be applied to improve an arbitrary agreed-upon policy in a cooperative partially observable game and proves that these search procedures are theoretically guaranteed to at least maintain the original performance of the agreed-Upon policy (up to a bounded approximation error).

core.title: Stable-Predictive Optimistic Counterfactual Regret Minimization
core.summary: This work presents the first CFR variant that breaks the square-root dependence on iterations, and shows that this method is faster than the original CFR algorithm, although not as fast as newer variants, in spite of their worst-case $O(T^{-1/2})$ dependence on iteration.

core.title: Knowledge Graph Programming with a Human-in-the-Loop: Preliminary Results
core.summary: The knowledge graph programming user experience is described, the language encourages users to mention knowledge graph entities in their programs, thus enabling the data compiler to exploit the extensive factual and type structure present in modern KGs.

core.title: Solving Imperfect-Information Games via Discounted Regret Minimization
core.summary: This paper introduces novel CFR variants that 1) discount regrets from earlier iterations in various ways, 2) reweight iterations inVarious ways to obtain the output strategies, 3) use a non-standard regret minimizer and/or 4) leverage "optimistic regret matching".

core.title: Can One Class Hour Improve Creative Problem Solving Self-efficacy
Deep Counterfactual Regret Minimization
core.summary: Deep Counterfactual Regret Minimization is introduced, a form of CFR that obviates the need for abstraction by instead using deep neural networks to approximate the behavior of CFR in the full game.

core.title: Depth-Limited Solving for Imperfect-Information Games
core.summary: A principled way to conduct depth-limited solving in imperfect-information games by allowing the opponent to choose among a number of strategies for the remainder of the game at the depth limit, which defeats two prior top agents using only a 4-core CPU and 16 GB of memory.

core.title: Superhuman AI for heads-up no-limit poker: Libratus beats top professionals
core.summary: Libratus, an AI that, in a 120,000-hand competition, defeated four top human specialist professionals in heads-up no-limit Texas hold’em, the leading benchmark and long-standing challenge problem in imperfect-information game solving is presented.

core.title: Libratus: The Superhuman AI for No-Limit Poker
core.venue: International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence
core.summary: This work presents Libratus, the first--and so far only--AI to defeat top human professionals in Heads-up no-limit Texas Hold'em.

core.title: The Impact of Bedside Interdisciplinary Rounds on Length of Stay and Complications
core.summary: Bedside IDR did not reduce overall LOS or clinical deterioration and future studies should examine whether comprehensive transformation of medical units, including co‐leadership, geographic cohorting of teams, and bedside interdisciplinary rounding, improves clinical outcomes compared to units without these features.

core.title: Reduced Space and Faster Convergence in Imperfect-Information Games via Pruning
core.summary: It is proved that when using CFR in zero-sum games, adding BRP will asymptotically prune any action that is not part of a best response to some Nash equilibrium, which leads to provably faster convergence and lower space requirements.

core.title: Safe and Nested Subgame Solving for Imperfect-Information Games
core.summary: This work introduces subgame-solving techniques that outperform prior methods both in theory and practice and shows that subgame solving can be repeated as the game progresses down the game tree, leading to far lower exploitability.

core.title: Baby Tartanian8: Winning Agent from the 2016 Annual Computer Poker Competition

core.summary: This work demonstrates a winning agent from the 2016 Annual Computer Poker Competition, Baby Tartanian8, which is the primary benchmark for evaluating game-solving algorithms for imperfect-information games.

core.title: Strategy-Based Warm Starting for Regret Minimization in Games
core.summary: This work introduces the first general, principled method for warm starting CFR, which requires only a strategy for each player, and accomplishes the warm start at the cost of a single traversal of the game tree.

core.summary: A distributed version of the most commonly used equilibrium-finding algorithm, counterfactual regret minimization (CFR), is introduced, which enables CFR to scale to dramatically larger abstractions and numbers of cores and a family of post-processing techniques that outperform prior ones are introduced.

core.title: Regret-Based Pruning in Extensive-Form Games
core.summary: An improvement to CFR is introduced that prunes any path of play in the tree, and its descendants, that has negative regret, and revisits that sequence at the earliest subsequent CFR iteration where the regret could have become positive, had that path been explored on every iteration.

core.title: Simultaneous Abstraction and Equilibrium Finding in Games
core.venue: International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence
core.summary: This work introduces a method that combines abstraction with equilibrium finding by enabling actions to be added to the abstraction at run time, which allows an agent to begin learning with a coarse abstraction, and then to strategically insert actions at points that the strategy computed in the current abstraction deems important.

core.title: G519 A novel three-tiered approach to improving paediatric education for general practice doctors and trainees
core.summary: A novel three-tiered education programme for qualified GPs and GP trainees that addresses the imbalance of Paediatric experience in GP training when compared to the Paediatrics proportion of a typical GP’s workload is designed.

core.summary: The results showed that there was not a statistically significant difference between those groups using the software and those that did not, however, the results did show that the software could have a positive impact on student conceptual understanding.

core.title: Regret Transfer and Parameter Optimization
core.summary: This work proves that regrets on actions in one setting (game) can be transferred to warm start the regrets for solving a different setting with same structure but different payoffs that can be written as a function of parameters, and provides the first principled warm-starting method for no-regret learning.
